en.title: Lanterns Series Hints at Guy Gardner's Wild Path to Green Lantern
en.summary: A recent episode of the popular Lanterns series may have finally shed light on a long-standing DC Comics mystery. The show appears to explain how Guy Gardner, with his distinctive haircut, became Earth's Green Lantern over other potential candidates.
en.body:
For years, fans of the Green Lantern Corps have pondered a peculiar point in the DC timeline: how did the brash, often abrasive **Guy Gardner** end up as Earth's Green Lantern, especially when characters like **John Stewart** seemed like more obvious choices? A recent episode of the **Lanterns** series appears to have finally offered an in-universe explanation, tying together threads from different eras of DC storytelling.

The series primarily navigates events set in 2016 and 2026, with occasional flashbacks. This contrasts with the timeline of the **Superman** movie, believed to be set around 2025. In 2016, we see **Hal Jordan** actively training **John Stewart** to succeed him as Earth's Green Lantern. However, by the time of the **Superman** film, **Guy Gardner** is clearly established as the Lantern. Since the lore dictates that Earth can only have one Green Lantern at a time, something significant must have occurred between these periods to shift the mantle. The latest **Lanterns** episode seems to have illuminated this pivotal moment, explaining what opened the door for **Guy Gardner**.

## The Haircut's Canonical Clue

The debate over **Guy Gardner**'s place in the Green Lantern hierarchy is a long-standing one, often fueled by his unique personality and, of course, his iconic bowl haircut. While the **Lanterns** series episode addresses the *why* of his becoming the Lantern, the *how* of his distinctive hairstyle has its own canonical roots. This particular look was officially explained in **Superman Unlimited #8**, a detail that cemented a long-running fan joke into official DC canon. It’s a quirky origin that underscores **Guy Gardner**’s status as a character who often defies conventional expectations, even in his appearance.

## Fan Reaction and the Gardner Enigma

This revelation is more than just a plot point for long-time comic readers; it’s a satisfying nod to decades of character development and fan discussion. **Guy Gardner** has always been a divisive figure, loved for his rebellious spirit and sometimes reviled for his arrogance. The idea that his path to becoming a Lantern might have been less straightforward than others, and that even his most recognizable physical trait has a specific, albeit humorous, origin, adds layers to his character. For fans who grew up with **Guy Gardner**, seeing these elements acknowledged and explained within a major on-screen adaptation is a significant moment, validating their passion for the character and the intricate tapestry of the DC Universe.

## What's Next

With the **Lanterns** series continuing to explore the wider Green Lantern mythology and its connections to other DC properties, fans can anticipate further revelations. The explanation for **Guy Gardner**'s ascension suggests that the series is committed to delving into the lore and answering long-held questions about the Corps and its Earth-based members.

Pictures *Note: This article contains spoilers for Lanterns and Superman (2025) So, quite a lot happened in Lanterns ‘ fifth episode. So much so, in fact, that it’s easy enough to overlook the ways that episode seemingly helped explain why we ended up with Guy Gardner as Earth’s protector over other, seemingly more obvious candidates. First, some timeline housekeeping. Lanterns largely portrays events that occur in two key years: 2016 and 2026 (with some flashbacks to earlier events). The timeline of the 2025 Superman movie is somewhat vague, but it’s believed to be set sometime around the year 2025 based on its relation to related releases. So, in 2016, Hal Jordan is training John Stewart to be Earth’s new Green Lantern. Yet, in Superman , we see that Guy Gardner is clearly the Green Lantern. Since Hal tells us that Earth can only have one protector at a time, something clearly happened between the events of those stories. Until now, though, we haven’t known what might have opened the door for Guy to take over. However, this last Lanterns episode seemingly helps solve the mystery. At the end of that episode (and many, many notable events), we see John Stewart take Hal’s ring but give it back to the Guardians rather than choose to work with the organization. Now, that is clearly not the end of Stewart’s story. There are three more episodes of Lanterns left, and we also know that Stewart will appear in Man of Tomorrow . Seemingly, he will serve the Green Lantern Corps in that movie, though it’s not entirely clear how that comes to pass. What we can reasonably assume for the moment, though, is that Stewart’s decision at the end of this episode leaves Earth without a protector. And then we come to Guy Gardner and his haircut . Earth needs a Green Lantern after Stewart turns the job down. That could leave an opening for Guy to take over. He is seemingly still in that role by the time that the events of Superman play out. As for why Guy Gardner is in that position in the first place… that remains a bit of a mystery. For what it’s worth, the comics argue that Guy was one of the original choices to become Earth’s Green Lantern, but Hal Jordan happened to be closer to the site of the crash that brought the alien Abin Sur (and his ring) to Earth.
